note: One profile per neighbourhood or town, written from what is on the site. `minutesFromHome` is recomputed from wherever you are.

items.name: Palo Alto
items.famousFor: Stanford, the HP Garage, and the downtown Silicon Valley grew up around
items.cafe: Goodthing on Ramona — the upstairs loft, and the Einspänner
items.bakery: Mademoiselle Colette on Lytton — the almond croissant
items.culture: The Cantor and the Rodin garden at Stanford — both free
items.park: Gamble Garden, two and a half acres off Waverley, free and rarely busy
items.unusual: The HP Garage on Addison Avenue, the birthplace of Silicon Valley, seen from the sidewalk
items.food: The Saturday farmers’ market on Gilman Street, there since 1983
items.walk: Ramona Street → University Avenue → Addison Avenue for the HP Garage
items.hidden: The Baylands boardwalk at dawn, a quarter of a mile over the marsh to open water

items.name: Menlo Park
items.famousFor: Kepler's Books and the Santa Cruz Avenue high street
items.cafe: Café Borrone, next door to Kepler's since 1989
items.bakery: Mademoiselle Colette on Santa Cruz Avenue
items.culture: Kepler's — the Peninsula's counterculture bookshop since 1955, with a serious events programme

items.name: Mountain View
items.famousFor: Castro Street and the Computer History Museum
items.culture: The Computer History Museum on Shoreline Boulevard
items.park: Shoreline Park — the lake, and the bay trail out over the marshes

items.name: Los Altos
items.famousFor: A small-town Main Street, a few minutes from everything that is not
items.culture: Linden Tree Books, the children's bookshop on State Street
items.food: Chef Chu's, open since 1970 on San Antonio Road

items.name: Mission
items.famousFor: Murals, taquerías, Dolores Park and the coffee that started San Francisco on specialty
items.cafe: Ritual on Valencia, the room that started the city on specialty coffee in 2005
items.bakery: Tartine on Guerrero — the morning bun, and it sells out
items.park: Dolores Park — the city lies on this hill on any warm afternoon
items.unusual: Balmy Alley, one block of murals repainted by Mission artists for decades
items.food: La Taqueria on Mission Street — ask for the burrito dorado
items.walk: 24th Street → Balmy Alley → up Valencia → Dolores Park

items.name: North Beach
items.famousFor: Little Italy, the Beats, and City Lights
items.bakery: Good Mong Kok on Stockton — dim sum by the piece, cash, point through the glass
items.culture: City Lights, the bookshop Lawrence Ferlinghetti founded in 1953
items.food: Tommaso's on Kearny — the first wood-fired pizza oven on the West Coast, lit in 1935
items.walk: Washington Square → Filbert Street → the Filbert Steps → Coit Tower
items.hidden: The Filbert Steps — wooden stairs down Telegraph Hill through cottage gardens

items.name: Hayes Valley
items.famousFor: Patricia's Green and the independent shops of Hayes Street
items.park: Patricia's Green, built where the freeway used to be
items.culture: The symphony and the opera, a block away at Civic Center

items.name: Inner Richmond
items.famousFor: Clement Street, and the north side of Golden Gate Park
items.culture: Green Apple Books on Clement, since 1967, new and used shelved together
items.park: Golden Gate Park, a few blocks south

items.name: Outer Sunset
items.famousFor: Ocean Beach, fog, and the surf end of the city
items.cafe: Andytown on Taraval — ask for a Snowy Plover
items.park: Ocean Beach, three miles of it
items.hidden: Sutro Baths and Lands End, at the north end of the beach

items.name: Cow Hollow
items.famousFor: Union Street, and the Marina and the waterfront below it
items.hidden: The Wave Organ, at the end of the jetty — the sea plays it at high tide

items.name: Cupertino
items.famousFor: Apple Park, the ring-shaped headquarters, and the town around it
items.culture: The Apple Park Visitor Center, with a roof terrace looking across to the ring
items.park: Rancho San Antonio, where half the valley walks at weekends, up to the deer and the farm
items.food: Gochi on Homestead Road for Japanese small plates, and ramen at Marufuku

items.name: Santa Clara
items.famousFor: Levi's Stadium, Santa Clara University and the old mission at its heart
items.culture: Mission Santa Clara de Asís, the rebuilt mission church on the university campus
items.unusual: California's Great America, the rollercoaster park beside the stadium

items.name: Santana Row
items.famousFor: An outdoor European-style street of restaurants and shops, and the South Bay's night out
items.walk: Santana Row end to end in the evening, when the patios fill
items.unusual: The Winchester Mystery House, Sarah Winchester's endless mansion with stairs to nowhere, ten minutes' walk away

items.name: Downtown San José
items.famousFor: The Bay Area's biggest city: the SAP Center, San Pedro Square and a downtown of museums
items.culture: The Tech Interactive and the San José Museum of Art, facing each other across Plaza de César Chávez
items.park: Guadalupe River Park, a long green strip along the river
items.food: San Pedro Square Market, a covered food hall with a courtyard

items.name: Willow Glen
items.famousFor: A leafy old San José neighbourhood with its own small-town main street
items.walk: Lincoln Avenue, cafés and independent shops under the trees

items.name: Campbell
items.famousFor: A restored downtown of restaurants and bars on Campbell Avenue
items.food: The Sunday farmers' market on Campbell Avenue
items.park: The Los Gatos Creek Trail, running through town down to Los Gatos

items.name: Los Gatos
items.famousFor: A pretty foothill town at the foot of the Santa Cruz Mountains
items.park: Vasona Lake, and the creek trail up to Lexington Reservoir
items.walk: North Santa Cruz Avenue → Main Street, then onto the creek trail

items.name: Saratoga
items.famousFor: A quiet hillside village and two famous gardens
items.culture: Montalvo Arts Center, an Italianate villa with concerts on the lawn in summer
items.park: Hakone Estate and Gardens, a Japanese garden from 1917
items.walk: Big Basin Way, the village's one main street of wine bars and restaurants

items.name: Woodside
items.famousFor: Horse country in the hills, redwoods, and Buck's, where Silicon Valley does its deals
items.park: Huddart Park, redwood trails above the town
items.culture: Filoli, a country house with sixteen acres of formal gardens

items.name: Portola Valley
items.famousFor: Open space and the oldest tavern around, the Alpine Inn
items.food: Burgers and a pitcher in the creekside beer garden at Rossotti's Alpine Inn
items.park: Windy Hill, the climb for the view over the whole bay
